title: Two papers disagree (diet-and-mortality)
explanation: Claim A finds no significant overall association between alcohol consumption and incident stroke, whereas Claim B reports that higher alcohol consumption is linearly associated with an increased stroke risk.
a_text: Alcohol consumption is not significantly associated with overall incident stroke compared with non-drinking (pooled adjusted RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.06).
b_text: Higher alcohol consumption is roughly linearly associated with a higher risk of stroke (HR 1.14 per 100 g/week higher consumption).

audit.reason: Both are meta-analyses of adult drinkers with comparable methods; an older pooled null vs a newer IPD's linear positive slope. Direct disagreement on whether an aggregate association exists.
audit.topic: alcohol / stroke — is there an association?
audit.basis: builder's hand review against the source abstracts (venue, method, population, dose, outcome)
